questions.prompt: A 3x3 smoothing kernel has all nine weights equal to 0.12. What happens to the mean brightness of a filtered image?
options: It falls because smoothing removes detail
It rises by about 8% because the weights sum to 1.08
It stays the same because every pixel is averaged
It depends only on the padding mode
questions.explanation: Weights sum to 9*0.12=1.08, so a constant region is scaled by 1.08.

questions.prompt: An image has 80 rows. A 7x7 kernel is applied in 'valid' mode with stride 1. How many rows does the output have? (integer)
Pixels carry independent noise with standard deviation 12 grey levels. After a 3x3 box filter (all weights 1/9), what is the noise standard deviation? (precision 0.01)
Correlate x=[1,2,4,7,11] with k=[-1,0,1] in valid mode. What is the second output value? (integer)
A 16x16 checkerboard with 1-pixel squares is reduced to 8x8 by keeping every second pixel in both directions. What does the result show?
options: A uniform image of one value, although the true mean is 0.5
A random-looking noise pattern made of the lost pixels
A smaller checkerboard that again has 1-pixel squares, just halved
A uniform grey of 0.5, the average of the two square colours
questions.explanation: Positions with even y and even x all have the same colour.

questions.prompt: Stripes with period 5 pixels are subsampled by keeping every 3rd pixel. What is the apparent period in the small image, in small-image pixels? (precision 0.1)
questions.explanation: f=0.2 cycles/px; sampled every 3: 0.6 per new px, alias |0.6-1|=0.4, period 2.5.

questions.prompt: A 4K image is reduced to 640 pixels wide for a detector. Explain why simply keeping every sixth pixel is a bad choice and what you do instead, including a sensible Gaussian sigma.
rubric: Names aliasing: content above the new Nyquist limit folds into false lower-frequency patterns.
Low-pass filter first (Gaussian with sigma about 0.5 x factor, or area averaging) and then subsample.
Notes the trade-off: some real detail is lost, nearest neighbour is only for label masks.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
